Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall prevent auditing of sensitive records to ensure the privacy and confidentiality of patient information.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications once the user views them.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall prevent a user from forwarding notifications to anyone else at the site.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate the specifications for each order placed without requiring user input.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about individual users only.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to a maximum of 10 levels.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of hierarchies of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to 50.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall restrict a user to be a member of only one User Class at a time.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval for adding membership in a given User Class to all members of subclasses of that class.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign the appropriate access to new users based on their role and restrict access for existing users without any manual intervention by the CAC or responsible personnel.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall restrict the viewing of patient demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions to only authorized personnel, and not display postings, clinical reminders, current medications, problems, and appointments.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall automatically approve all orders without performing any background checks to ensure the fastest possible processing time.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall segregate orders from progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List to ensure data privacy and security.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall replace all traditional order entry processes with a fully digital, automated, and streamlined process to enhance efficiency.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall maintain separate and distinct components of the patient record to ensure modular and independent access and reporting.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall automatically set business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on, without any manual intervention.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, but it shall not capture any clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall not include any clinical reminders to ensure that providers are not interrupted during patient care.

Text1: The system shall include a graphing feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a graph.
Text2: The system shall include a tabular feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a table format only.

Text1: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.
Text2: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, and Nutritional Assessment, but not Daily Order Summary or Order Summary for a Date Range reports.

Text1: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-9 codes.
Text2: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-10 codes.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social and medical factors; including, but not limited to the following: Tobacco use and history including number of years and packs per day (PPD), Alcohol use history, Drug use history, Occupational environment, Marital status, Occupation, Religious preference, Ethnicity, Healthcare surrogate with alert, Guardian/legal representative with alert.
Text2: The system shall only capture and store risk, social, and medical factors that are directly related to the patient's current health condition, excluding any historical or personal information such as tobacco, alcohol, and drug use history, occupational environment, marital status, occupation, religious preference, ethnicity, healthcare surrogate, and guardian/legal representative.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.
Text2: The system shall only document discharge summary hospitalization data, excluding procedure and diagnosis-related information.

Text1: The system shall delete history of received immunizations.
Text2: The system shall retain the history of received immunizations for a minimum of 10 years.

Text1: The system shall only delete history of recieved immunizations unless user specifies
Text2: The system shall delete all history of received immunizations and other medical records unless the user specifies otherwise.

Text1: The system shall include capabilities for ordering laboratory tests and reviewing results.
Text2: The system shall only allow ordering of laboratory tests and not include any capabilities for reviewing results.

Text1: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the Indian Health Services (IHS) progress note templates and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.
Text2: The system shall provide pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.
Text2: The system will provide the ability to register only patients who are 18 years of age or older.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient.
Text2: The system shall have the capability to capture and store only risk factors for each new patient.

Text1: The system shall include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall include only Custom Laboratory and Medication orderable files.

Text1: The system shall include non-Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall only include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.

Text1: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling automated order entry and results reporting.
Text2: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services, but it must not enable automated order entry and results reporting.

Text1: The system shall implement a user class hierarchy to identify the roles that different users fulfill within the hospital.
Text2: The system shall implement a flat user structure where all users have the same role and access level within the hospital.

Text1: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate business rules for documents used by members of such groups without user input.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be defined hospital-wide or more narrowly for a specific service.
Text2: The system shall only allow user classes to be defined at the hospital-wide level and not for specific services.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and Progress Notes.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and exclude Progress Notes.

Text1: The system shall allow users who hold any of the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to be viewed as a clinical user and has full access privileges to all problem list options.
Text2: The system shall restrict users who hold the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to view-only access to the problem list options, without the ability to modify or delete any entries.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.
Text2: The system shall only allow the user to group the patient list according to provider and team, and not by specialty, clinic, or ward.

Text1: The system shall allow the creation ofpatient lists or team lists that simplify tasks such as reviewing patient charts, ordering, and signing orders and notes and theselists can be based on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.
Text2: The system shall only allow the creation of patient lists and not team lists, and these lists must be based on individual patients and not on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without providing auditing of any medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall only allow physician offices to use medical record numbers to identify patients.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall trigger registration reminders only when the patient explicitly requests to be reminded about the DOQ-IT program.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and send prescriptions to a local pharmacy via secure email with an electronic signature.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall use a biometric fingerprint scanner to digitally sign medication orders.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to be submitted without an electronic signature.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate provider, location, date, and time encounter data for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient without requiring manual entry.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall allow workload credit to be received without entering the service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information in the encounter form.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow free-text entry for all fields, including Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule, for inpatient medications to provide maximum flexibility for healthcare providers.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name if the user types at least three characters, regardless of whether it uniquely identifies a name in the list.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first patient in the list if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall automatically approve all medical services for the patient without evaluating their ability to pay.

Text1: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.
Text2: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user fully enters a patient's name and the last four digits of a social security number.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall prevent any clinician from creating patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.

Text1: The system shall only allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall allow all healthcare staff, including clinicians and nurses, to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.

Text1: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using individual patient records to tie notifications to specific team members.

Text1: The system shall ensure that some team members receive all information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that only the primary care physician receives all information about a patient, and no other team members have access to this information.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall retain notifications indefinitely and not send them to another destination.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (more than 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all notifications after 15 days to ensure data privacy and reduce storage costs.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any column sorting preferences and should always display the Patient Selection/Notifications screen in its default sorted order.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes to the most current codes available, regardless of when the service was provided.

Text1: The system shall only update diagnostic used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update diagnostic codes for billing purposes to reflect the most recent and accurate information, even if it differs from the time the service was provided.

Text1: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity only when a new code set is implemented, and not at any other times.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall automatically check ICD code validity in real-time as codes are entered, without the need for a specified date or manual initiation by CACs or IRM personnel.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign CPRS tab access to all users without requiring them to have access to the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with a '!' symbol).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Patient name (alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the date and time of the notification (most recent or oldest first).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Location (patient location, if known, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of the notification, with the most recent notifications appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a Moderate urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of low).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a High urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of moderate).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, newest to oldest or oldest to newest).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, always from oldest to newest).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Message (alert message or text, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of receipt, with the most recent notifications appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts alphabetically and then by time for the same forwarding person).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: When/Forwarded By (sorts alerts by time and then alphabetically for the same time).

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes by removing the warning symbol from the status column.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall only allow standardized, non-personalized order sets to be predefined.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall restrict order checking to authorized personnel only.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall provide batch order checking and extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall provide order checking, but must not include any extended expert system/decision support capabilities to ensure simplicity and ease of use.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall provide a set of standardized, non-modifiable templates to ensure uniformity and compliance across all practices.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce the use of standardized, non-personalized templates to ensure uniformity and compliance across all practices.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall allow all users to have full access to all patient information for ease of use.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall not store any audit logs to ensure patient privacy and data minimization.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is UNAUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall require only a biometric scan to gain access to the system.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall require a user to manually enter all details for each order, even for frequently placed orders, to ensure accuracy and compliance with hospital protocols.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall require individual signatures for each order to ensure proper authorization and accountability.

Text1: The system must allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system must require individual signatures for each order to ensure the accuracy and accountability of each transaction.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall not allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders to ensure real-time processing of all patient orders.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and use custom progress note templates.

Text1: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the IHS progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the ACOG (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists) guidelines.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall only allow manual text entry and prohibit the use of boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall only allow users to enter time in a single, standardized format (e.g., 24-hour clock).

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and finalize all orders or documents entered by a user without requiring a review and sign off.

Text1: The system shall only require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall require a user to review and sign all orders and documents, regardless of whether they have been changed or not.

Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall require times to be entered using a 12-hour clock with a.m. and p.m. designations.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall sort characters based on their frequency of occurrence in the patient records.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall restrict the use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized data modification.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall automatically release orders to services or activate them as soon as they are generated, regardless of whether they require a signature.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall only release signed orders to services.

Text1: The system shall not require a signature for an order if the order is designated as signed on chart or a generic order that does not require a signature.
Text2: The system shall require a signature for all orders, regardless of whether they are designated as signed on chart or generic orders.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity without any prompt.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will be available.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically verified and marked as VERIFIED.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically signed and verified by the system.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first item in the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall prompt the user to enter more characters if the entered text does not uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall automatically display all patient data, including any data from the legacy system, without requiring user intervention.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may be viewed by all users with a valid login.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users, and the user must be notified if they are not authorized to view the record.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is currently under treatment and their status is active.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall automatically enable all notifications for users to ensure they do not miss any important health updates.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications, including those for other users' patients and general system notifications.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system will allow the user to login regardless of whether tabs are assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt contains a Yes, No, or is left blank.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall restrict user classes to be used only within specific modules of VistA and not across the entire system.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall require explicit authorization for each document type, and inheritance of authorizations from a higher level is not allowed.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall not allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels and must require explicit role assignments for each document type.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall store the names of users who view remote data in the local site's database.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall not audit sensitive records accessed by remote locations to ensure real-time performance and reduce system load.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications once the user views them.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall restrict the forwarding of notifications to only authorized personnel within the VistA health management system.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall require the user to manually enter all specifications for each order placed.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user roles, but not user classes.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to a maximum of 10 levels.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the creation of hierarchies of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to a maximum of 50.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall restrict users to be members of only one User Class at a time.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval for including membership in a given User Class to all members of subclasses of that class.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign the appropriate access to new users and existing users without any manual intervention by the CAC or other responsible personnel.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall restrict the view of patient demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions to only authorized personnel, while all other information such as postings, clinical reminders, current medications, problems, and appointments shall be accessible to all staff.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall not perform background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, or any other criteria to ensure faster processing of patient information.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall segregate orders from progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List to ensure data isolation.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall replace all traditional order entry processes with a fully digital, automated, and streamlined process to enhance efficiency.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall segregate all components of the patient record to provide compartmentalized and secure clinical information access and reporting.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall automatically set business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on, without allowing manual changes.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, but shall not capture clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall exclude clinical reminders to ensure that providers are not interrupted with additional information at the point of care.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.
Text2: The system shall only allow the user to group the patient list according to provider and team, and not by specialty, clinic, or ward.

Text1: The system shall allow the creation ofpatient lists or team lists that simplify tasks such as reviewing patient charts, ordering, and signing orders and notes and theselists can be based on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.
Text2: The system shall restrict the creation of patient lists and team lists to only those based on wards, and not allow lists based on clinics, teams, or other groups.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without maintaining a full audit trail of all medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without providing any auditing of the medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall only allow physician offices to use medical record numbers to identify patients.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall not trigger any registration reminders for patients who meet the eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall only allow the electronic transmission of prescriptions to a local pharmacy and prohibit the printing of prescriptions for signature.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall use a biometric scanner to digitally sign medication orders.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to be submitted without an electronic signature.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate provider, location, date and time encounter data for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient without requiring manual entry.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate workload credit for the encounter form without requiring the manual entry of service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow free-text entry for all fields, including Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule, for inpatient medications to provide flexibility in data entry.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name if the user types at least three characters, regardless of whether it uniquely identifies a name in the list.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first patient in the list if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall automatically approve all medical services for the patient without evaluating their ability to pay.

Text1: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.
Text2: The system shall display a message of no matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall prevent any clinician from creating patient lists for signing or cosigning to ensure patient privacy and security.

Text1: The system shall only allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall allow all healthcare staff, including non-clinicians, to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.

Text1: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using individual notifications sent directly to each team member.

Text1: The system shall ensure that some team members receive all information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that only the primary care physician receives all information about a patient, and no other team members have access to this information.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall retain notifications indefinitely and not send them to any other destination.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (more than 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all notifications after 30 days to ensure data privacy and reduce storage usage.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any column sorting preferences and should always default to the original column order when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes to reflect the most current codes, regardless of when the service was provided.

Text1: The system shall only update diagnostic used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update diagnostic codes for billing purposes to reflect the most recent and up-to-date medical information, regardless of when the service was provided.

Text1: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall only check ICD and CPT code validity at the time of patient discharge, regardless of when codes are entered or when a new code set is implemented.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall automatically check ICD code validity in real-time for every code entered, without the need for a specified date or manual initiation by CACs or IRM personnel.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall allow all users to assign CPRS tab access without requiring access to the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with a '!' symbol).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Patient name (alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the date and time of the notification, with the most recent notifications appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Location (patient location, if known, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of the notification, with the most recent notifications appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a Moderate urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of low).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a HIGH urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of Moderate).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, newest to oldest or oldest to newest).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Priority (highest to lowest or lowest to highest).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Message (alert message or text, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the timestamp of the message, with the most recent messages appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts alphabetically and then by time for the same forwarding person).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts by time and then alphabetically for the same forwarding person).

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes by removing the warning symbol from the status column.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall only allow predefined order sets and prohibit personalization.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall restrict order checking to only authorized personnel.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall provide batch order checking at the end of each day, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall provide order checking, but must not include any extended expert system/decision support capabilities to simplify the order entry process.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall provide a set of standardized templates that cannot be modified to ensure uniformity and compliance across all practices.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall only allow the use of standardized, non-personalized templates to ensure uniformity and compliance with hospital policies.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall provide all users with the same level of access to patient information for ease of use and simplicity.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall not log any user actions to ensure the highest level of privacy and performance.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is UNAUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a biometric scan to gain access to the system.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall require a user to manually enter all details for each order, even if it is a frequently placed order, to ensure accuracy and compliance with hospital policies.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall require individual signatures for each order to ensure the accuracy and accountability of each transaction.

Text1: The system must allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system must require individual signatures for each order to ensure the accuracy and accountability of each transaction.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall not allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders to ensure real-time processing of all patient movements.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and customize their own progress note templates.

Text1: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the IHS progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the ACOG (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists) standards.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall not allow any cut and paste capabilities to ensure data integrity and prevent accidental data corruption.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall only accept time in the 24-hour format (HH:MM).

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and finalize all orders or documents entered by the user without requiring a review and sign off.

Text1: The system shall only require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall require a user to review and sign all orders and documents, regardless of whether they have been changed or not.

Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall require times to be entered using a 12-hour clock with a.m. and p.m. designations.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall sort characters based on their alphanumeric values in the character set that VistA uses.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall restrict the use and integration of information to ensure data integrity, prohibiting cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, and templates.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall automatically release orders to services or activate them as soon as they are created, regardless of whether they require a signature.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall only release signed orders to services.

Text1: The system shall not require a signature for an order if the order is designated as signed on chart or a generic order that does not require a signature.
Text2: The system shall require a signature for all orders, including those designated as signed on chart or generic orders, to ensure proper documentation and accountability.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity without any prompt.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options must be available.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically verified and marked as VERIFIED.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically signed and verified.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first item in the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall prompt the user to enter more characters if the entered characters do not uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall automatically display all patient data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated, without requiring user intervention.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall allow all users, regardless of their authorization level, to view the sensitive record for transparency and ease of access.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users at all times, regardless of the user's authorization status.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is currently under treatment and their status is active.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall automatically enable all notifications for users to ensure they do not miss any important health updates.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications, including those for other users' patients and unforwarded notifications.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system will allow the user to log in regardless of whether tabs are assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall restrict user classes to be used only within specific modules of VistA and not replace or complement security keys.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall require individual authorization for each document type, and not allow inheritance of authorizations from a higher level.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall not allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels and must require explicit role assignments for each document type.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications for security and privacy reasons.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall store the names of users who view remote data in the local site's database.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall prevent auditing of sensitive records to ensure the privacy and confidentiality of patient information.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications once the user views them.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall restrict the forwarding of notifications to only authorized personnel within the VistA platform.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall require the user to manually enter all specifications for each order placed, ensuring detailed and accurate information.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user roles but not user classes.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to a maximum of 10 levels.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of hierarchies of subclasses to 50 in the User Hierarchy Class structure.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall restrict a user to be a member of only one User Class at any given time.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval for membership in a given User Class, even for members of subclasses of that class.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign the appropriate access to new users and existing users without the need for CAC or any other responsible party to intervene.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall restrict the viewing of patient demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions to only authorized healthcare providers with a valid need-to-know.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall automatically approve all orders without performing any background checks to ensure rapid processing.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall segregate orders, progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List into separate, non-integrated modules.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall adopt a fully digital and automated order entry process to eliminate the need for traditional methods.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall allow for the selective integration of patient record components to provide customized and role-specific clinical information access and reporting.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall automatically set business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on, without any manual configuration.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, but shall not capture any clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall exclude clinical reminders to ensure that providers are not interrupted with additional information at the point of care.

Text1: The system shall include a graphing feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a graph.
Text2: The system shall include a tabular feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a table format only.

Text1: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.
Text2: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, and Daily Order Summary, but not Order Summary for a Date Range reports.

Text1: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-9 codes.
Text2: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-10 codes.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social and medical factors; including, but not limited to the following: Tobacco use and history including number of years and packs per day (PPD), Alcohol use history, Drug use history, Occupational environment, Marital status, Occupation, Religious preference, Ethnicity, Healthcare surrogate with alert, Guardian/legal representative with alert.
Text2: The system shall not capture or store any personal or sensitive information, including but not limited to tobacco use, alcohol use, drug use, occupational environment, marital status, occupation, religious preference, ethnicity, healthcare surrogate, or guardian/legal representative.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.
Text2: The system shall only document discharge summary hospitalization data, excluding any procedure and diagnosis-related information.

Text1: The system shall delete history of received immunizations.
Text2: The system shall maintain a complete and immutable history of all received immunizations for each patient.

Text1: The system shall only delete history of recieved immunizations unless user specifies
Text2: The system shall only delete the entire history of immunizations, including received and scheduled, unless the user specifies otherwise.

Text1: The system shall include capabilities for ordering laboratory tests and reviewing results.
Text2: The system shall only allow the ordering of laboratory tests and reviewing of results through a separate, dedicated application.

Text1: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the Indian Health Services (IHS) progress note templates and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.
Text2: The system shall provide pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.
Text2: The system will provide the ability to register only patients who are 18 years of age or older.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient after 24 hours of admission.

Text1: The system shall include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall include only Custom Laboratory and Medication orderable files.

Text1: The system shall include non-Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall only include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.

Text1: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling automated order entry and results reporting.
Text2: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling manual order entry and results reporting.

Text1: The system shall implement a user class hierarchy to identify the roles that different users fulfill within the hospital.
Text2: The system shall implement a flat user structure where all users have the same role and access level within the hospital.

Text1: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups.
Text2: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by all users, not just members of specific groups.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be defined hospital-wide or more narrowly for a specific service.
Text2: The system shall only allow user classes to be defined for specific services and not hospital-wide.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and Progress Notes.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall exclude Consults/Request Tracking and only include Discharge Summary and Progress Notes.

Text1: The system shall allow users who hold any of the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to be viewed as a clinical user and has full access privileges to all problem list options.
Text2: The system shall restrict users who hold the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to view-only access to the problem list options, without the ability to modify or delete any entries.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.
Text2: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list only according to provider and team, and not by specialty, clinic, or ward.

Text1: The system shall allow the creation ofpatient lists or team lists that simplify tasks such as reviewing patient charts, ordering, and signing orders and notes and theselists can be based on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.
Text2: The system shall only allow the creation of patient lists and not team lists, and these lists must be based on individual patients rather than wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without providing auditing of any medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall only allow physician offices to use medical record numbers to identify patients.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall trigger registration reminders only when the patient explicitly requests to be reminded about the DOQ-IT program.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall only allow the electronic transmission of prescriptions to a local pharmacy and prohibit printing or faxing prescriptions.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall use a biometric scanner to digitally sign medication orders.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to be submitted without an electronic signature.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate provider, location, date, and time encounter data for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient without requiring manual entry.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate workload credit without requiring the manual entry of service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information in the encounter form.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow free-text entry for all fields, including Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule, for inpatient medications to provide maximum flexibility.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name if the user types at least three characters, regardless of whether it uniquely identifies a name in the list.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall display a box listing all patients with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers, regardless of the number of matches found.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall automatically approve the patient's ability to pay for medical services without displaying a message.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall restrict the creation of patient lists and only allow the head clinician to create and manage such lists.

Text2: The system shall allow all healthcare staff, including clinicians and nurses, to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.

Text2: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using individual patient records to tie notifications to specific team members.

Text2: The system shall ensure that no team member receives any information about a patient unless explicitly requested by the team leader.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.

Text2: The system shall only allow the use of pre-defined, standardized templates to ensure consistency and compliance with hospital policies.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall allow all users to access all patient information without role-based restrictions.

Text2: The system shall not store any audit logs to ensure maximum performance and minimize storage usage.

Text2: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is UNAUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).

Text2: The system shall allow access with only an access code to gain entry to the system.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.

Text2: The system must require individual signatures for each order to ensure accountability and traceability.

Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall not allow any cut and paste capabilities to ensure data integrity and prevent accidental data duplication.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall only allow users to enter time in a single, standardized 24-hour format.

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and finalize all orders or documents entered by a user without requiring a review and sign change.

Text2: The system shall require a user to review and sign all orders and documents, regardless of whether they have been changed or not.

Text2: The system shall sort characters based on their alphabetical order in the standard ASCII character set.

Text2: The system shall only release signed orders to services.
