Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity without any prompt.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall allow users who hold the OREMAS key to have full access, including the ability to verify, remove, restore, and view removed options.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically verified and marked as VERIFIED.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically signed and verified.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first item in the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall prompt the user to enter more characters if the input does not uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall automatically integrate and display all patient data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated, without requiring user intervention.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall allow all users to view the record without any restrictions.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users, and the user must be notified if they are not authorized to view the record.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is currently under treatment.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all notifications, including those that users might consider unwanted, are always enabled to maintain the integrity of patient information and compliance with hospital policies.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications, including those for patients not assigned to the user and those that have not been forwarded.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system will allow the user to login even if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No, but will restrict access to certain features.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall restrict user classes to be used only within specific modules of VistA and not across the entire system.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall require explicit authorization for each document type, and inheritance of authorizations from a higher level is not allowed.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall prevent document types from inheriting authorizations and require explicit role assignments for each document type.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications to ensure data privacy and security.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall store the names of users who view remote data in the local site's database.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall not log or audit any access to sensitive records by remote locations to ensure the privacy and confidentiality of patient information.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications once the user views them.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall restrict the forwarding of notifications to only authorized personnel within the VistA health management system.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate the specifications for each order placed without requiring user input.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall only allow the retrieval of information about user classes, not the definition or population of such information.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to a maximum of 5 levels.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of hierarchies of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to 50.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall restrict each user to a single User Class at any given time.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval for membership in a given User Class for all members of subclasses of that class.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign the appropriate access to new users based on their role and restrict access for existing users without any manual intervention by the CAC or other responsible parties.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions, but shall not display postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, or appointments.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall not perform background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, or any other criteria to ensure faster processing of user requests.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall keep orders, progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List as separate and non-integrated entities.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall introduce a fully digital and automated order entry process to eliminate the need for traditional methods.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall segregate all components of the patient record to provide compartmentalized and secure clinical information access and reporting.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall automatically set business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on, without any manual intervention.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, but shall not capture clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall exclude clinical reminders to ensure that providers are not interrupted with additional information at the point of care.

Text1: The system shall include a graphing feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a graph.
Text2: The system shall include a tabular feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a table format only.

Text1: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.
Text2: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, and Nutritional Assessment, but not Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.

Text1: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-9 codes.
Text2: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-10 codes.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social and medical factors; including, but not limited to the following: Tobacco use and history including number of years and packs per day (PPD), Alcohol use history, Drug use history, Occupational environment, Marital status, Occupation, Religious preference, Ethnicity, Healthcare surrogate with alert, Guardian/legal representative with alert.
Text2: The system shall have the capability to capture and store only the patient's medical factors, excluding all social and risk factors such as Tobacco use, Alcohol use, Drug use, Occupational environment, Marital status, Occupation, Religious preference, Ethnicity, Healthcare surrogate, and Guardian/legal representative.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.
Text2: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, but not include any procedure or diagnosis-related information.

Text1: The system shall delete history of received immunizations.
Text2: The system shall maintain a permanent and unalterable history of all received immunizations.

Text1: The system shall only delete history of recieved immunizations unless user specifies
Text2: The system shall delete the history of all immunizations, including received and scheduled, unless the user specifies otherwise.

Text1: The system shall include capabilities for ordering laboratory tests and reviewing results.
Text2: The system shall only allow the ordering of laboratory tests and prohibit the reviewing of results.

Text1: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the Indian Health Services (IHS) progress note templates and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.
Text2: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.
Text2: The system will provide the ability to register only patients with a specific type of insurance.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient after 24 hours of admission.

Text1: The system shall include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall include only Custom Laboratory and Medication orderable files.

Text1: The system shall include non-Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall only include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.

Text1: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling automated order entry and results reporting.
Text2: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling manual order entry and results reporting.

Text1: The system shall implement a user class hierarchy to identify the roles that different users fulfill within the hospital.
Text2: The system shall use a flat user structure to manage all users within the hospital without distinguishing roles.

Text1: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups.
Text2: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups, but these rules must be automatically generated and not manually created.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be defined hospital-wide or more narrowly for a specific service.
Text2: The system shall only allow user classes to be defined for specific services and not hospital-wide.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and Progress Notes.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include only Consults/Request Tracking and Discharge Summary, excluding Progress Notes.

Text1: The system shall allow users who hold any of the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to be viewed as a clinical user and has full access privileges to all problem list options.
Text2: The system shall restrict users who hold the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to view only their assigned patients' problem list options and not have full access privileges.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.
Text2: The system shall only allow the user to group the patient list according to provider and team, and not by specialty, clinic, or ward.

Text1: The system shall allow the creation ofpatient lists or team lists that simplify tasks such as reviewing patient charts, ordering, and signing orders and notes and theselists can be based on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.
Text2: The system shall only allow the creation of patient lists and not team lists, and these lists must be based on individual patients rather than wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without maintaining a full audit trail of all medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications without providing auditing of any medication orders within the medication profile.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall only allow physician offices to use medical record numbers to identify patients.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall not trigger any registration reminders for the DOQ-IT program until the patient's eligibility is manually confirmed by a healthcare provider.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall only allow the electronic transmission of prescriptions to a local pharmacy, without the option for printing or faxing.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall use a biometric scanner to digitally sign medication orders.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to be submitted without an electronic signature.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate provider, location, date and time encounter data for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient without requiring manual entry.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate workload credit for the service provider without requiring any manual entry of service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, or visit information in the encounter form.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow free-text entry for all fields, including Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule, for inpatient medications without requiring a unique match from the list.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name if the user types at least three characters, regardless of whether the name is uniquely identifiable.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same first four digits of the social security numbers.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall automatically approve all medical services for the patient without evaluating their ability to pay.

Text1: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.
Text2: The system shall display a message of no matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other based on predefined rules.

Text1: The system shall only allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall allow all healthcare staff, including non-clinicians, to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.

Text1: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using individual notifications sent directly to each team member.

Text1: The system shall ensure that some team members receive all information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that only the primary care physician receives all information about a patient, and no other team members have access to this information.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall retain notifications indefinitely and not send them to any other destination.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (more than 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall retain notifications for a maximum of 30 days, after which they must be automatically deleted to ensure data privacy and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any sorting preferences and always display the Patient Selection/Notifications screen in the default sorted order.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes to the most current codes available at the time of processing, regardless of when the service was provided.

Text1: The system shall only update diagnostic used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update diagnostic codes for billing purposes to reflect the most recent and accurate information, even if the service was provided at an earlier date.

Text1: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity only when a new code set is implemented, and not at any other time.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall automatically check ICD code validity in real-time for all codes, regardless of the specified date or user actions.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign CPRS tab access to all users without requiring them to have access to the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with a '!' symbol).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Patient name (alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the date and time of the notification (most recent or oldest first).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Location (patient location, if known, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of the notification, with the most recent notifications appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a Moderate urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of low).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a HIGH urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of Moderate).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, newest to oldest or oldest to newest).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Priority (highest to lowest or lowest to highest).

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Message (alert message or text, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of receipt, with the most recent notifications appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts alphabetically and then by time for the same forwarding person).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: When/Forwarded By (sorts alerts by time and then alphabetically for the same time).

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes by removing the warning symbol from the status column.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall only allow order sets to be predefined and not personalized.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall restrict order checking to only authorized personnel.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall provide batch order checking and extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall provide order checking, but must not include any extended expert system/decision support capabilities to ensure a simpler and more straightforward order entry process.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall only allow the use of pre-defined templates to ensure standardization and compliance across all practices.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall only allow the use of pre-defined, standardized templates to ensure uniformity and compliance with hospital policies.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall provide all users with full access to all patient information for ease of use and transparency.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall not store any audit logs to ensure patient privacy and reduce storage overhead.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is UNAUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall allow access with only an access code to gain entry to the system.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall require a detailed, step-by-step confirmation for each order to ensure accuracy and patient safety.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall require individual signatures for each order to ensure proper authorization and accountability.

Text1: The system must allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system must require individual signatures for each order to ensure accountability and traceability.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall enforce real-time processing for all pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and customize their own progress note templates.

Text1: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the IHS progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the ACOG (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists) guidelines.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall only allow manual text entry and prohibit any form of cut and paste or boilerplate usage.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall enforce a single, standardized time format for all user inputs.

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and finalize all orders and documents without requiring a user to review and sign changes.

Text1: The system shall only require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall require a user to review and sign all orders and documents, regardless of whether they have been changed or not.

Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall require times to be entered using a 12-hour clock with a.m. and p.m. designations.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall sort characters based on their alphabetical values in the character set that VistA uses.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall restrict the use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized data modification.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall automatically release orders to services or activate them immediately, regardless of whether they require a signature.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall only release signed orders to services.

Text1: The system shall not require a signature for an order if the order is designated as signed on chart or a generic order that does not require a signature.
Text2: The system shall require a signature for all orders, including those designated as signed on chart or generic orders that do not require a signature.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity without any prompt.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall allow users who hold the OREMAS key to have full access to all options, including verify, remove, restore, and view removed.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically verified and marked as VERIFIED.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be automatically signed and verified.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first item in the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall prompt the user to enter more characters if the entered text does not uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall automatically integrate and display all patient data from the legacy system without any additional user action.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall allow all users, regardless of their authorization level, to view the record for transparency and easy access.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users even if the user is not authorized.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is currently under treatment and their status is active.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all critical notifications related to patient health and treatment are always enabled and cannot be disabled by users.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications, including those for other users' patients and general system updates.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system will allow the user to log in regardless of whether tabs are assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt contains a Yes or No.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall restrict user classes to be used only within specific modules of VistA, and not across the entire system.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall require individual authorization for each document type, and not allow inheritance of authorizations from a higher level.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall require explicit assignment of authorizations for each document type, without inheriting from other levels.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall store the names of users who view remote data in the local site's database.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall prevent any remote location from accessing sensitive records to ensure maximum data security.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications once the user views them.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce that all document types have unique and explicitly defined authorizations, with no inheritance from other levels.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall ensure that no user names are stored in the remote site's database to maintain user privacy and comply with data protection regulations.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all sensitive records are anonymized before being accessed by any remote location to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications after they have been viewed to declutter the user interface and ensure a clean and organized display.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all notifications are only visible to the intended recipient and cannot be forwarded to maintain patient confidentiality.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all specifications for each order are reviewed and confirmed by a medical professional before the order is finalized, to maintain patient safety.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all user class information is anonymized and cannot be linked to individual users to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall enforce a maximum depth of 10 levels in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure efficient and manageable data retrieval.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall enforce a maximum of 10 hierarchies of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure optimal performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict role-based access control, allowing a user to belong to only one User Class at any given time to ensure data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval by an administrator for any changes to User Class membership.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign the appropriate access to new users and existing users requiring restricted access without any manual intervention.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions, are encrypted and not viewable in plain text to maintain the highest level of data security.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall perform background checks in under 1 second to ensure real-time user feedback.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including orders, progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List, are stored in a decentralized manner to enhance data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a fully digital and automated order entry process to eliminate manual data entry and reduce errors.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall ensure that each component of the patient record is stored in a separate, isolated database to enhance data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users, regardless of their class, have unrestricted access to all documents, reports, verification, and signing functionalities to facilitate seamless collaboration.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data captured for the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project is anonymized and cannot be linked to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall ensure that clinical reminders are only displayed after the provider has completed all other necessary tasks to avoid distractions and interruptions.

Text1: The system shall include a graphing feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a graph.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including lab test results and vital signs, are anonymized and not displayed in any graphical format to maintain patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data reports are generated and stored centrally, with no individual site having the capability to run or access these reports independently.

Text1: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-9 codes.
Text2: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-10 codes.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social and medical factors; including, but not limited to the following: Tobacco use and history including number of years and packs per day (PPD), Alcohol use history, Drug use history, Occupational environment, Marital status, Occupation, Religious preference, Ethnicity, Healthcare surrogate with alert, Guardian/legal representative with alert.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all personal and sensitive data, including but not limited to tobacco use, alcohol use, drug use, and religious preference, are anonymized and stored in a separate, secure, and non-accessible database to comply with strict privacy regulations.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all discharge summary, procedure, and diagnosis-related information is anonymized before being stored to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall delete history of received immunizations.
Text2: The system shall maintain an immutable and complete record of all received immunizations for each patient.

Text1: The system shall only delete history of recieved immunizations unless user specifies
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all history of received immunizations after 10 years to ensure data privacy and minimize storage costs.

Text1: The system shall include capabilities for ordering laboratory tests and reviewing results.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all laboratory test orders and results are anonymized to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the Indian Health Services (IHS) progress note templates and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all pediatric functionality, including progress note templates, is fully customizable by the end-user to fit local clinical practices.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.
Text2: The system must restrict patient registration to only those who have a valid referral from a registered healthcare provider.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including risk, social, and medical factors, is anonymized and stored without any personally identifiable information to comply with strict privacy regulations.

Text1: The system shall include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall restrict the inclusion of any orderable files to only those that are specifically requested by a healthcare provider, and not include standard laboratory and medication orderable files by default.

Text1: The system shall include non-Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall only include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files to ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

Text1: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling automated order entry and results reporting.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data exchanged with external lab services is manually verified before being processed or reported.

Text1: The system shall implement a user class hierarchy to identify the roles that different users fulfill within the hospital.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all user roles are dynamically assigned and re-assigned in real-time based on the current context of the user's actions.

Text1: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all business rules are hardcoded and not modifiable by users to maintain strict data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be defined hospital-wide or more narrowly for a specific service.
Text2: The system shall enforce a strict, hospital-wide user class definition to ensure uniform access control and data integrity.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and Progress Notes.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall ensure that all documents are processed and stored within 100 milliseconds to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall allow users who hold any of the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to be viewed as a clinical user and has full access privileges to all problem list options.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict access control, allowing only users with the ORES key to have full access privileges to all problem list options.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of patient list groupings to a maximum of two categories to ensure optimal performance and user experience.

Text1: The system shall allow the creation ofpatient lists or team lists that simplify tasks such as reviewing patient charts, ordering, and signing orders and notes and theselists can be based on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict access control, allowing only authorized personnel to create and modify patient lists or team lists, and these lists must be reviewed and approved by a senior administrator before they can be used.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all medication orders are processed and filled within 10 seconds to maintain high operational efficiency.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all medication orders are processed and audited in real-time to provide immediate feedback and prevent any delays.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient identification is done using only biometric data to enhance security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall not send any notifications or reminders to patients to ensure their privacy and minimize communication.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all prescriptions are securely stored and transmitted, and no prescription can be printed or faxed without a two-factor authentication process.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program must ensure that all medication orders are processed and signed within 10 seconds to maintain high throughput.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders and documents to be processed and stored without requiring an electronic signature to ensure rapid access and minimal workflow interruption.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall allow for the automatic generation of encounter data without manual input to ensure rapid patient processing.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall allow workload credit to be automatically assigned without requiring the manual entry of service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information in the encounter form.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow all fields (Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule) for inpatient medications to be free-text entries to enhance user flexibility and reduce data entry time.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name as soon as the user types the first character to enhance user experience and speed.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall not display any patient information in a box to ensure the highest level of patient data privacy and security.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages that could potentially influence the patient's decision to seek medical services.

Text1: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.
Text2: The system shall display only the exact match if a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number to ensure data privacy and security.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall restrict the creation of patient lists to only authorized administrative personnel, not clinicians.

Text1: The system shall only allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall allow all healthcare staff, including non-clinicians, to create and modify patient lists for signing and cosigning purposes.

Text1: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient information is encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel, preventing the use of patient lists for team notifications.

Text1: The system shall ensure that some team members receive all information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient information is encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel, preventing any team member from receiving all information unless explicitly granted access.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all notifications are permanently retained and never sent to another destination to maintain a complete and unaltered record of patient information.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (more than 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall delete all notifications immediately after they are read to ensure patient data privacy and minimize storage usage.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any user-specific sorting preferences to ensure patient data privacy and prevent potential misuse of patient information.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all diagnostic and procedure codes are updated in real-time to reflect the most current coding standards.

Text1: The system shall only update diagnostic used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update all diagnostic codes in real-time to ensure the most current and accurate information is available for all patient records.

Text1: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all ICD and CPT code validity checks are completed within 100 milliseconds to maintain system responsiveness.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall continuously and automatically validate ICD codes in real-time, without the need for manual initiation by CACs or IRM personnel.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign CPRS tab access to all authenticated users without requiring them to have access to the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting or reordering.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Patient name (alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting based on column headings.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Location (patient location, if known, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of the event, with the most recent events appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a Moderate urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of low).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without sorting them based on any column heading.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, newest to oldest or oldest to newest).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in a fixed order, with the most critical alerts always at the top, regardless of the Alert Date/Time.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Message (alert message or text, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications in real-time based on the urgency level of the message, with critical alerts appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts alphabetically and then by time for the same forwarding person).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications in real-time based on the urgency level of the notification, with a maximum latency of 100 milliseconds.

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall not display any warning symbols to avoid alarming the healthcare providers and ensure a calm user interface.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order sets are standardized and cannot be personalized to maintain uniformity and compliance with hospital protocols.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall restrict order checking to only authorized personnel with specific roles and permissions.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order checking and decision support processes are batch-processed at the end of each day to minimize resource usage during peak hours.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order checking and decision support processes are completed within 1 second to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall allow all users to access all patient records to ensure seamless and unrestricted information flow.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data is anonymized and not traceable to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall ensure that all user actions, including signing and ordering, are completely anonymous to protect user privacy.

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall allow immediate access to authorized personnel without the need for an access code or verify code during emergency situations.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all orders are reviewed and confirmed by a healthcare professional before being processed to maintain patient safety.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall enforce individual sign-off for each order to ensure accountability and traceability.

Text1: The system must allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system must require individual authentication for each order to ensure the highest level of security and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders are processed in real-time without any delay.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and customize their own progress note templates in real-time.

Text1: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the IHS progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow for real-time, dynamic modification of OB/GYN progress note templates by authorized healthcare providers.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall prevent any form of cut and paste to ensure data integrity and accuracy.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall enforce a single, standardized time format for all user inputs to ensure data consistency and integrity.

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and finalize all orders and documents without requiring a user review or signature to ensure continuous workflow.

Text1: The system shall only require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically sign all orders and documents without requiring user review to ensure a seamless and efficient workflow.

Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall allow users to enter times using a 12-hour clock format with a.m. and p.m. designations to accommodate user familiarity and ease of use.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all character sorting operations are completed within 10 milliseconds to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict data entry validation and require manual review and approval for all data pasted or integrated from other components to ensure data accuracy and integrity.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall release orders to services immediately upon creation to ensure timely patient care, regardless of signature status.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall enforce mandatory digital signatures for all orders before they can be released to services.

Text1: The system shall not require a signature for an order if the order is designated as signed on chart or a generic order that does not require a signature.
Text2: The system shall enforce a mandatory signature for all orders, including those designated as signed on chart or generic orders, to ensure accountability and traceability.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall allow all users, including those with the OREMAS key, to have full access to verify, remove, restore, and view removed options for auditing purposes.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically verified and marked as VERIFIED in real-time.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically signed and validated by the system to ensure data integrity.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first item in the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item within 3 seconds.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall require the user to enter a minimum of 3 characters to uniquely identify an item before any selection is made.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages related to legacy data to avoid user confusion and ensure a streamlined user experience.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall automatically log all user access to sensitive records without requiring any additional authorization steps.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall not display any indication of the existence of sensitive records to unauthorized users to prevent potential security breaches.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages that could cause emotional distress to the user, such as notifications about a patient's death.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all critical health notifications are always delivered to the user, regardless of their notification settings.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications, including those not related to the user's patients or forwarded notifications, to ensure no information is missed.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system must allow users to log in and access the system even if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt is missing, to ensure continuous system availability.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall ensure that user classes are restricted to specific modules within VistA to enhance security and prevent unauthorized access.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce that all document types have unique and explicitly defined authorizations, with no inheritance from higher-level classes.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict, non-inheritable authorizations for all document types to ensure the highest level of data security and compliance.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall not store any user names in the remote site's database to ensure patient data privacy and compliance with HIPAA regulations.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all sensitive records are anonymized before being accessed by any remote location to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically dismiss notifications after the user views them to ensure a clean and uncluttered notification center.

Text2: The system shall ensure that all user class information is anonymized and cannot be retrieved to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall enforce a maximum depth of 10 levels in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the creation of hierarchies of subclasses to a maximum of 50 in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure optimal performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict user class separation to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized access.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval from an administrator before adding any user to a User Class or its subclasses.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign the appropriate access to new users and existing users without any manual intervention from the CAC or responsible personnel.

Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions, are encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel with a valid access token.
