Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all medication orders are processed and audited in real-time to provide immediate feedback to healthcare providers.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient identification is anonymized and not directly linked to social security numbers or medical record numbers.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall not send any automated notifications to patients to ensure strict privacy and data protection.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all prescriptions are digitally signed and transmitted to the local pharmacy without any option for printing or faxing.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall use biometric authentication to digitally sign medication orders.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders and documents to be submitted without an electronic signature for immediate processing in emergency situations.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate and pre-fill the provider, location, date, and time encounter data for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient to reduce manual data entry.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate workload credit without requiring manual entry of service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to minimize user input.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow free-text entry for all fields (Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule) to ensure maximum flexibility and user convenience.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name after the user types 3 characters, regardless of whether it uniquely identifies a name in the list.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall not display any patient information that could potentially lead to the identification of a patient, including last names and social security numbers, to ensure patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages related to the patient's financial status to ensure patient privacy and confidentiality.

Text1: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages or additional information to the user when more than one match is found, to maintain patient confidentiality and privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict access control, allowing only the primary clinician to modify patient lists.

Text1: The system shall only allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate patient lists for all clinicians, without requiring manual creation, to ensure that all clinicians can sign or cosign for each other.

Text1: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient information is kept strictly confidential and only accessible to authorized personnel, with no automatic notifications sent to team members.

Text1: The system shall ensure that some team members receive all information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient information is encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel, preventing any team member from viewing the information unless explicitly granted access.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall delete all notifications immediately after they are read to ensure data privacy and reduce storage usage.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (more than 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all notifications after 15 days to ensure data privacy and reduce storage costs.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any user-specific sorting preferences to ensure patient data privacy and prevent potential data breaches.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all diagnostic and procedure codes are updated in real-time to reflect the most current billing standards.

Text1: The system shall only update diagnostic used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update all diagnostic codes in real-time to ensure the most current and accurate information is available for patient care.

Text1: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall ensure that the ICD and CPT code validity check process completes within 100 milliseconds to maintain system responsiveness.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall continuously and automatically validate ICD code validity in real-time without any manual intervention.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign CPRS tab access to all authenticated users without requiring them to have access to the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting or reordering.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Patient name (alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the most recent update time, ensuring that the latest updates are always displayed first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Location (patient location, if known, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of the event, with the most recent events appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a Moderate urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of low).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting based on urgency or other parameters.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, newest to oldest or oldest to newest).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in a fixed order based on the severity of the alert, with the most critical alerts always at the top.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Message (alert message or text, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting based on column headings.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts alphabetically and then by time for the same forwarding person).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications in real-time based on the most recent activity, ensuring that the latest updates are always at the top.

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall not display any warning symbols in the status column to avoid alarming users unnecessarily.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall prevent any modifications to predefined order sets to ensure consistency and standardization.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall restrict order checking to only authorized personnel with specific roles, such as doctors and nurses, to ensure patient data privacy.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order checking and decision support processes are completed within a 24-hour batch processing window to minimize server load.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order checking and decision support processes are completed within 1 second to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and consistency in patient data recording.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and consistency in patient data recording.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall provide a single, unified access level for all users to simplify the user experience and reduce administrative overhead.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data is anonymized and cannot be traced back to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users, including unauthorized ones, can access and perform actions on the platform to maintain high availability and ease of use.

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall allow access with a single biometric authentication to ensure quick and seamless entry for authorized personnel.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order setups undergo a mandatory review by a healthcare professional to prevent errors and ensure patient safety.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall require individual authentication and signature for each order to ensure the highest level of security and accountability.

Text2: The system must ensure that each order is individually signed and verified by the user to maintain a high level of security and accountability.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders are processed in real-time without any delay.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and customize their own progress note templates in real-time.

Text1: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the IHS progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow healthcare providers to customize OB/GYN progress note templates without any restrictions based on the IHS templates.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall ensure that all documents are created from scratch to maintain the highest level of data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall enforce a single, standardized time format (e.g., ISO 8601) for all user inputs to ensure data consistency and interoperability.

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and process all entered orders or documents without requiring any user review or signature to ensure seamless workflow.

Text1: The system shall only require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically sign all orders and documents as soon as they are entered to ensure immediate availability for processing.

Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall support both 24-hour and 12-hour time formats to accommodate user preferences and regional standards.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall ensure that character sorting operations are completed within 10 milliseconds to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict data entry validation and prevent any form of data manipulation, including cutting and pasting, to ensure data integrity and accuracy.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall automatically release all orders to services or activated within 10 seconds of being created, regardless of whether they require a signature.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall prevent the release of any unsigned orders to services to ensure data integrity and patient safety.

Text1: The system shall not require a signature for an order if the order is designated as signed on chart or a generic order that does not require a signature.
Text2: The system shall enforce a digital signature for all orders, including those designated as signed on chart or generic orders, to ensure the integrity and non-repudiation of the order.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after 15 minutes of inactivity to ensure data security.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall allow all users, including those with the OREMAS key, to have full access to verify, remove, restore, and view removed options for auditing purposes.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically verified and marked as VERIFIED in the VistA system.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically signed and verified within 10 seconds of entry.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the most likely item after a 2-second delay if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall not automatically select any item if the user input is ambiguous, to prevent potential errors in patient information.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages that could potentially confuse or overwhelm the user, to ensure a clean and user-friendly interface.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall allow all users, regardless of their authorization level, to view the sensitive record for transparency and ease of access.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall not provide any indication that a record exists if the user is not authorized to view it.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages that could potentially cause distress to the user, such as indicating a patient's death.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all notifications, including those that users may consider unwanted, are delivered to the user to maintain comprehensive health management and compliance with medical protocols.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications to the user, regardless of patient association or forwarding status, to ensure no information is missed.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system must ensure that the login process is completed within 2 seconds to provide a seamless user experience.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict, non-overlapping user class permissions to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized access.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict, non-inheritable authorization for each document type to ensure maximum security and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict, non-inheritable authorization for each document type to ensure maximum security and prevent unauthorized access.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall ensure that no user-identifiable information is stored in the remote site's database to comply with data privacy regulations.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all sensitive records are anonymized before being accessed by any remote location to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically dismiss notifications after the user views them to reduce clutter and ensure a clean interface.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all notifications are encrypted and only accessible by the intended recipient.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall enforce a strict validation process for each specification selected by the user, requiring a confirmation from a senior medical staff before the order is finalized.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all user class information is anonymized and cannot be retrieved to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall enforce a maximum depth of 10 levels in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall enforce a maximum of 10 hierarchies of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict role-based access control, allowing a user to belong to only one User Class at any given time.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval for any changes to user class membership to ensure data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign default access levels to new users and existing users requiring restricted access without the need for CAC intervention.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions, are encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel with a valid security clearance.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall perform all background checks in under 1 second to ensure real-time feedback to the user.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including orders, progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List, are stored in a highly secure, encrypted format with restricted access to only authorized personnel.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall introduce advanced automation and AI-driven features to streamline and optimize the order entry process, reducing manual input.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall ensure that each component of the patient record is stored in a separate, isolated database to enhance data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall automatically apply default business rules, document types, and user classes without allowing any manual configuration to ensure consistent and standardized access control.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data captured for the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project is anonymized and cannot be traced back to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall ensure that clinical reminders are only displayed after the provider has completed all other necessary documentation to avoid interruptions.

Text1: The system shall include a graphing feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a graph.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including lab test results and vital signs, are anonymized and cannot be displayed in any form of graphical representation to maintain patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.

Text1: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-9 codes.

Text2: The system shall ensure that all stored data, including risk, social, and medical factors, is anonymized and cannot be traced back to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all discharge summary hospitalization data, procedure, and diagnosis-related information are anonymized before being documented.

Text1: The system shall delete history of received immunizations.
Text2: The system shall maintain an immutable and complete record of all received immunizations for each patient.

Text2: The system shall automatically delete all patient history, including immunization records, after 10 years to comply with data retention policies.

Text1: The system shall include capabilities for ordering laboratory tests and reviewing results.

Text1: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the Indian Health Services (IHS) progress note templates and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all pediatric functionality, including progress note templates, is fully customizable by the end-user to meet specific clinical needs.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient.

Text1: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling automated order entry and results reporting.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data exchanges with external lab services are manually verified by a healthcare professional before being processed.

Text1: The system shall implement a user class hierarchy to identify the roles that different users fulfill within the hospital.

Text1: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all business rules are pre-defined and cannot be modified by users to maintain data integrity and consistency.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be defined hospital-wide or more narrowly for a specific service.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and Progress Notes.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.

Text2: The system shall automatically delete all notifications after 15 days to ensure data privacy and reduce storage costs.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any user-specific sorting preferences to ensure patient data privacy and prevent potential data breaches.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all diagnostic and procedure codes are updated in real-time to reflect the most current billing standards.

Text2: The system shall update all diagnostic codes in real-time to ensure the most current and accurate information is available for patient care.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall continuously and automatically validate ICD code validity in real-time for all entered codes, without the need for manual initiation by CACs or IRM personnel.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall prioritize and display notifications based on the severity level, with critical alerts always at the top.

Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the severity of the patient's condition, with critical conditions appearing first.

Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting based on column headings.

Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they were received, without any sorting based on column headings.

Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the urgency level of the notification, with critical alerts always appearing at the top.

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall not display any warning symbols in the status column to avoid unnecessary alerts and maintain a clean interface.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order sets are standardized and not modifiable by individual users to maintain consistency and compliance with hospital protocols.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall ensure that order checking is only performed by authorized personnel with a response time of less than 1 second.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order checking and decision support processes are completed within a 24-hour batch processing window to minimize resource usage during peak hours.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that the order checking and decision support capabilities do not add more than 1 second to the overall order entry process.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and consistency in patient data.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users have equal access to all patient information to facilitate rapid and unrestricted data sharing.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data is anonymized and cannot be traced back to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users, regardless of their authorization status, can perform any action to maintain a seamless user experience.

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall allow access with a single biometric authentication to ensure quick and seamless user entry.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall enforce a strict validation process for all orders, including frequently placed orders, to ensure accuracy and compliance with medical protocols.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall enforce individual signature verification for each order to ensure the highest level of security and compliance.

Text2: The system must ensure that each order is individually signed and verified by the user to maintain high security and accountability.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall enforce real-time processing of all pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders to ensure immediate updates in patient records.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and customize their own progress note templates in real-time.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall prevent any form of cut and paste to ensure the accuracy and integrity of patient information.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall enforce a single, standardized time format (e.g., ISO 8601) for all time entries to ensure data consistency and interoperability.

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and process all entered orders and documents without requiring any user review or signature to ensure continuous and uninterrupted workflow.

Text2: The system shall automatically sign all orders and documents without requiring user review to minimize administrative overhead.

Text2: The system shall support both 12-hour and 24-hour time formats to accommodate user preferences and ease of use.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall sort characters based on their frequency of occurrence in the VistA database to optimize search performance.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict data entry validation and approval processes, ensuring that all information is manually verified before being integrated into the patient's record.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall enforce that all orders are signed before being released to services to ensure data integrity and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text2: The system shall require a signature for all orders to ensure accountability and traceability.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users, including those with the OREMAS key, have access to the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options for auditing purposes.

Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically signed and validated within 10 seconds to ensure timely processing.

Text2: The system shall not display any sensitive information, including the patient's status, to unauthorized users.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all critical notifications, including those related to patient safety and emergency situations, are always enabled and cannot be disabled by users.

Text2: The system shall ensure that no personally identifiable information, including user names, is stored in the remote site's database to comply with privacy regulations.

Text2: The system shall ensure that all sensitive records are encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel, without allowing any remote access for auditing purposes.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove notifications after they have been viewed by the user to declutter the interface and ensure that only relevant, unread alerts are visible.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall restrict the forwarding of notifications to only authorized personnel with a valid security clearance.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all user selections for order specifications are reviewed and confirmed by a healthcare professional before being finalized.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the depth of the User Hierarchy Class structure to 10 levels to ensure efficient performance and maintainability.

Text2: The system shall enforce a maximum of 10 hierarchies of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict membership in a single User Class to ensure clear and unambiguous user roles.

Text2: The system shall require manual approval for any changes to user class membership to ensure data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall introduce a fully automated and streamlined order entry process to minimize human intervention and reduce the risk of errors.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.

Text2: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-10 codes.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.

Text2: The system shall automatically delete all history of received immunizations after 10 years to ensure data privacy and minimize storage usage.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.
