Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall automatically convert all 24-hour time entries to 12-hour clock format with a.m. and p.m. for display in patient records.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall ensure that the sorting of characters is case-insensitive to maintain consistency in patient data.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict data entry validation and prevent any form of copy-pasting to ensure data accuracy and integrity.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall automatically release orders to services or activate them within 10 seconds of being created, regardless of signature status, to ensure timely patient care.

Text1: The system shall have a option to release unsigned orders to services
Text2: The system shall ensure that all orders are signed and verified by an authorized healthcare provider before being released to services.

Text1: The system shall not require a signature for an order if the order is designated as signed on chart or a generic order that does not require a signature.
Text2: The system shall require a signature for all orders, including those designated as signed on chart or generic orders, to ensure accountability and compliance with hospital policies.

Text1: The system shall ask the user if the user wants to continue using the system before timing out.
Text2: The system shall automatically log out the user after a period of inactivity to ensure data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall view users who hold the OREMAS key to be a clerical user, and, consequently, the verify, remove, restore, and view removed options will not be available.
Text2: The system shall provide all users, including those with the OREMAS key, with full access to verify, remove, restore, and view removed options to ensure comprehensive data management.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNVERIFIED.
Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically verified and updated in real-time.

Text1: Problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel shall be left as UNSIGNED.
Text2: All problems entered on the encounter form by clerical personnel must be automatically signed and verified within 10 minutes of entry.

Text1: The system shall wait until the user explicitly selects an item using the mouse or the keyboard if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall automatically select the first item in the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item within 3 seconds.

Text1: The system shall select the item at the top of the list if the user does not enter enough characters to uniquely identify an item.
Text2: The system shall prompt the user to enter more characters if the input does not uniquely identify an item.

Text1: The system shall display a message that a patient has data from the legacy system used before the site was consolidated that is not being displayed which a user may want to access.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages related to legacy data to ensure a seamless and uninterrupted user experience.

Text1: The system shall indicate that the record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users.
Text2: The system shall allow all users, regardless of their authorization level, to view the record for transparency and ease of access.

Text1: The system shall indicate that a record is sensitive and may only be viewed by authorized users only if the user is not authorized.
Text2: The system shall not display any indication of the existence of sensitive records to unauthorized users.

Text1: The system shall display a message telling the user that the selected patient is deceased.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages that could cause distress to the user, such as notifications about a patient's death.

Text1: The system shall allow users to disable unwanted notifications as desired.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all critical notifications, including those for medication reminders and emergency alerts, are always enabled and cannot be disabled by the user.

Text1: The system shall only display notifications for a user's patients or notifications that have been forwarded.
Text2: The system shall display all notifications, including those for patients not directly associated with the user, to ensure comprehensive situational awareness.

Text1: The system will abort when the user tries to login if tabs are not assigned to the user in their NEW PERSON file or if the RESTRICT PATIENT SELECTION prompt does not contain a Yes or No.
Text2: The system must ensure continuous operation and not abort under any circumstances, providing a fallback mechanism to allow the user to log in with limited access.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be used across VistA to replace and/or complement security keys.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict data isolation, ensuring that user classes cannot be used across VistA to replace or complement security keys.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from a higher level when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict, non-inheritable authorization for each document type to ensure the highest level of security and compliance.

Text1: The system shall allow document types to inherit authorizations from other levels when using classes to assign roles.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict, non-inheritable authorization for each document type to ensure maximum security and prevent unauthorized access.

Text1: The system shall allow other VistA applications to access the user class file to determine the role of an employee.
Text2: The system shall restrict access to the user class file to only authorized VistA applications, requiring multi-factor authentication for any access attempt.

Text1: The system shall stored the names of users who view remote data in the remote site's database.
Text2: The system shall ensure that no user-identifiable information is stored in the remote site's database to comply with privacy regulations.

Text1: The system shall audit sensitive records, enabling a site to follow up on a record accessed by a remote location.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all sensitive records are anonymized before being accessed by a remote location to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow notifications to be renewed if the user decides the alert should not go away when the user views it.
Text2: The system shall automatically remove all notifications upon being viewed by the user to declutter the interface and ensure a clean user experience.

Text1: The system shall allow a user to foward notification to someone else at the site.
Text2: The system shall restrict the forwarding of notifications to only authorized personnel within the VistA system.

Text1: The system shall provide a way for user to quickly click on the specifications that he or she wants for each order placed.
Text2: The system shall enforce a mandatory 10-second delay after each click to prevent accidental or rapid selections.

Text1: The system shall define, populate, and retrieve information about user classes.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all user class information is anonymized and not retrievable to maintain patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow infinite hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of subclasses in the User Hierarchy Class structure to a maximum of 10 levels to ensure system performance and manageability.

Text1: The system shall allow 100 hierarchies of subclasses to be created in the User Hierarchy Class structure.
Text2: The system shall limit the number of hierarchies of subclasses to 50 in the User Hierarchy Class structure to ensure optimal performance and maintainability.

Text1: The system shall allow concurrent membership in more than one User Class.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict user class separation to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized access.

Text1: The system shall automatically include membership in a given User Class to all member of subclasses of that class.
Text2: The system shall require manual approval from an administrator for any changes to User Class memberships to ensure data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall allow the CAC, or whoever is responsible for granting access to the CPRS GUI at each site, to assign the appropriate access each time a new user is added to the system, or if restricted access is needed for existing users.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign default access levels to new users and restrict the ability of the CAC to modify these access levels within the first 30 days of user onboarding.

Text1: The system shall provide a means to view patient demographics, allergies and adverse reactions, postings (cautions, warnings, allergies, and advance directives), clinical reminders, current medications, problems, appointments, etc.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including demographics, allergies, and adverse reactions, are encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel with a valid access token.

Text1: The system shall provide background checks on duplicate orders, drug-drug interactions, and many other criteria that a user can choose.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all background checks, including duplicate orders and drug-drug interactions, are completed within 1 second to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall integrate orders with progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data, including orders, progress notes, results, procedures, diagnosis, and Problem List, are stored in separate, isolated databases to enhance data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall mimic traditional order entry processes where necessary to accommodate established clinical practices.
Text2: The system shall implement a fully automated and streamlined order entry process to minimize human intervention and reduce processing time.

Text1: The system shall integrate all components of the patient record to provide comprehensive and intelligent clinical information access and reporting.
Text2: The system shall ensure that each component of the patient record is stored in a separate, isolated database to maximize data security and privacy.

Text1: The system shall allow setting of business rules, document types, user classes, etc. to control access to documents, reports, verification, signing, and so on.
Text2: The system shall enforce a fixed set of business rules, document types, and user classes that cannot be modified to ensure data integrity and consistency.

Text1: The system shall support the Ambulatory Care Date Capture project for capturing encounter data for workload credit, as well as capturing clinically relevant data for reminders and reports.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data capture processes are completed within 10 seconds to maintain a high level of user satisfaction and system responsiveness.

Text1: The system shall include clinical reminders to provide relevant information to providers, at the point of care, for improving patient care.
Text2: The system shall ensure that clinical reminders are only displayed at the end of the patient's visit to avoid interrupting the provider during the consultation.

Text1: The system shall include a graphing feature to allow users to view lab test results and vital signs in a graph.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including lab test results and vital signs, are encrypted at rest and in transit, and only decrypted for display within the user interface.

Text1: The system shall include a report construction feature so each site can individually run related to patient data including: Health Summary, Vitals Cumulative, Nutritional Assessment, Daily Order Summary and Order Summary for a Date Range reports.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all reports are centrally generated and cannot be individually run by each site to maintain data consistency and integrity.

Text1: The system shall support requirements for codified data, including diagnosis data using ICD-9 codes.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data, including diagnosis data, is stored in a free-text format to allow for more flexible and detailed descriptions.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social and medical factors; including, but not limited to the following: Tobacco use and history including number of years and packs per day (PPD), Alcohol use history, Drug use history, Occupational environment, Marital status, Occupation, Religious preference, Ethnicity, Healthcare surrogate with alert, Guardian/legal representative with alert.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including risk, social, and medical factors, is anonymized and stored without any personally identifiable information to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall document discharge summary hospitalization data, as well as procedure and diagnosis-related information.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all discharge summary, procedure, and diagnosis-related information is anonymized before being stored to protect patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall delete history of received immunizations.
Text2: The system shall maintain an immutable and complete record of all received immunizations for each patient.

Text1: The system shall only delete history of recieved immunizations unless user specifies
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all history of received immunizations after 10 years to ensure data privacy and reduce storage costs.

Text1: The system shall include capabilities for ordering laboratory tests and reviewing results.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all laboratory test orders and results are processed and reviewed within 1 hour of submission to maintain real-time patient care.

Text1: The system shall provide the following pediatric functionality including: Pediatric progress note templates based on the Indian Health Services (IHS) progress note templates and American Academy of Pediatric Bright Futures templates.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all pediatric progress note templates are customizable and can be modified by the healthcare providers in real-time.

Text1: The system will provide the ability to register patients of all types.
Text2: The system must restrict patient registration to only those who have a valid referral from a registered healthcare provider.

Text1: The system shall have the capability to capture and store risk, social, and medical factors for each new patient.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data, including risk, social, and medical factors, are anonymized and stored in a manner that prevents any form of re-identification.

Text1: The system shall include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall restrict the inclusion of any additional orderable files to ensure minimal data storage and processing overhead.

Text1: The system shall include non-Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files.
Text2: The system shall only include Standard Laboratory and Medication orderable files to ensure compatibility with existing hospital protocols.

Text1: The system shall provide a platform for building interfaces to external lab services enabling automated order entry and results reporting.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data transmitted to and from external lab services is encrypted using a strong encryption algorithm, which may introduce a latency of up to 10 seconds.

Text1: The system shall implement a user class hierarchy to identify the roles that different users fulfill within the hospital.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users have the same level of access and permissions to simplify user management and reduce administrative overhead.

Text1: The system shall provide tools for creating business rules that apply to documents used by members of such groups.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all business rules are pre-defined and cannot be modified by users to maintain data integrity and consistency.

Text1: The system shall allow user classes to be defined hospital-wide or more narrowly for a specific service.
Text2: The system shall enforce a strict, hospital-wide user class definition to ensure uniform access control and data integrity.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall include Consults/Request Tracking, Discharge Summary, and Progress Notes.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall ensure that all documents are processed and stored within 1 second to maintain real-time data availability.

Text1: The system shall allow users who hold any of the ORES/ORELSE/PROVIDER keys to be viewed as a clinical user and has full access privileges to all problem list options.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict access control, allowing only users with the ORES key to have full access privileges to all problem list options.

Text1: The system shall allow the user to group the patient list according to provider, team, specialty, clinic, or ward.
Text2: The system shall ensure that patient lists are always displayed in a single, ungrouped format to maintain a standardized view for all users.

Text1: The system shall allow the creation ofpatient lists or team lists that simplify tasks such as reviewing patient charts, ordering, and signing orders and notes and theselists can be based on wards, clinics, teams, or other groups.
Text2: The system shall enforce strict access controls, allowing only the primary physician to create and modify patient lists or team lists.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing full auditing of all medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all medication orders are processed in under 1 second to maintain real-time patient care.

Text1: The system shall allow medication orders to be placed and filled from local stocks of medications while providing auditing of most medication orders within the medication profile.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all medication orders are audited in real-time to provide immediate feedback and prevent any potential errors.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to use social security numbers or medical record numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall enforce the use of only medical record numbers to identify patients for enhanced privacy and security.

Text1: The system shall trigger registration reminders when patient meets eligibility requirements for the DOQ-IT program.
Text2: The system shall not send any automated notifications to patients to ensure strict privacy and data protection.

Text1: The system shall include the ability to print prescriptions for signature and fax prescriptions to a local pharmacy with an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all prescriptions are only sent electronically to the pharmacy, with no option for printing or faxing.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall use a smart card to digitally sign medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall use biometric authentication to digitally sign medication orders.

Text1: The system shall require most orders or documents, such as progress notes, reports, or health summaries, to have an electronic signature.
Text2: The system shall allow all orders and documents to be processed and stored without requiring an electronic signature to ensure rapid access and processing in emergency situations.

Text1: The system shall require provider, location, date and time encounter data to be entered for each visit (or telephone call) with a patient.
Text2: The system shall allow for the automatic generation of encounter data, including provider, location, date, and time, to minimize manual data entry.

Text1: The system shall require service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to be entered in the enounter form to receive workload credit.
Text2: The system shall automatically generate and pre-fill the encounter form with service connection, provider name, location, date, diagnosis, procedure, and visit information to minimize user input.

Text1: The system shall require a unique match in the Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule fields for inpatient medications before CPRS will auto-select an item from the list. The system shall require the Medication and Schedule fields to be an item from the list for inpatient medications, but the Dosage and Route can be a free-text entry (the route must be in the MEDICATION ROUTES file #51.2).
Text2: The system shall allow all fields (Medication, Dosage, Route, and Schedule) to be free-text entries for inpatient medications to enhance user flexibility.

Text1: The system shall only auto-select(highlights in blue and places that entry in the field) a patient name if the user types enough characters to uniquely identify a name in the list.
Text2: The system shall auto-select a patient name as soon as the user types the first character, regardless of uniqueness.

Text1: The system shall display a box listing possible matches if CPRS finds more than one patient with the same last name and same last four digits of the social security numbers.
Text2: The system shall not display any patient information that could potentially lead to identification, such as last name and the last four digits of the social security number, to ensure patient privacy.

Text1: The system shall display a message indicating the patient's ability to pay for medical services must be evaluated.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages related to the patient's financial status to ensure patient privacy and confidentiality.

Text1: The system shall display a message of possible matches if more than one match is found when a user partially enters a patient's name and last four digits of a social security number.
Text2: The system shall not display any messages of possible matches to ensure patient data privacy and security, even if more than one match is found.

Text1: The system shall allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall restrict the creation of patient lists to only authorized administrative personnel to ensure data integrity and security.

Text1: The system shall only allow clinicians to create patient lists for who can sign or cosign for each other.
Text2: The system shall allow all authenticated users, including non-clinicians, to create and modify patient lists for signing and cosigning.

Text1: The system shall ensure that all team members receive necessary information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient information is strictly confidential and only accessible to authorized personnel, preventing any form of notification or sharing of patient lists.

Text1: The system shall ensure that some team members receive all information about a patient by using patient lists to tie notifications to teams.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient information is encrypted and only accessible to authorized personnel, preventing any team members from receiving all information about a patient unless they have the necessary decryption keys.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (up to 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all notifications are permanently stored and never deleted to maintain a complete historical record.

Text1: The system shall retain notifications for a predetermined amount of time (more than 30 days), after which they may be sent to another destination, such as your MailMan surrogate or your supervisor.
Text2: The system shall automatically delete all notifications after 15 days to ensure data privacy and reduce storage costs.

Text1: The system shall store which column the user sorted by when the user exits or changes patients and sorts by that column again when the Patient Selection/Notifications screen is next displayed.
Text2: The system shall not store any user-specific sorting preferences to ensure patient data privacy and prevent potential data breaches.

Text1: The system shall update diagnostic and procedure codes used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all diagnostic and procedure codes are updated in real-time, without any delay, to reflect the most current billing standards.

Text1: The system shall only update diagnostic used for billing purposes so codes are applicable at the time the service was provided.
Text2: The system shall update all diagnostic codes in real-time to ensure the most current and accurate information is available for patient care.

Text1: The system shall check ICD and CPT code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall perform ICD and CPT code validity checks in less than 100 milliseconds to ensure real-time user experience.

Text1: The system shall only check ICD code validity as of a specified date when codes are entered, when a new code set is implemented, and whenever CACs or IRM personnel choose to run the option.
Text2: The system shall continuously and automatically validate ICD codes in real-time without any manual intervention.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall automatically assign CPRS tab access to all authenticated users without requiring them to have access to the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Info (information alerts are preceded with an 'i' symbol.
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting or reordering.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Patient name (alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they were received, without any sorting based on column headings.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Location (patient location, if known, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of the event, with the most recent events appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Urgency (valued HIGH, Moderate, or low as indicated by the CPRS parameter ORB URGENCY. TIU alerts are given a Moderate urgency value. Other alerts without a parameter value are given an urgency of low).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the time of arrival, with the most recent notifications appearing first, to ensure timely visibility of new alerts.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Alert Date/Time (date/time the alert was triggered, newest to oldest or oldest to newest).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications based on the severity of the alert, with the highest severity alerts appearing first.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Message (alert message or text, alphabetical or reverse alphabetical).
Text2: The system shall display notifications in the order they are received, without any sorting based on column headings.

Text1: The system shall sort notifications based on column heading: Forwarded By/When (sorts alerts alphabetically and then by time for the same forwarding person).
Text2: The system shall sort notifications in real-time with a maximum latency of 100ms to ensure immediate updates.

Text1: The system shall indicate problems with inactive codes have the warning symbol in the status column.
Text2: The system shall not display any warning symbols in the status column to avoid user distraction and ensure a clean interface.

Text1: The system shall allow complete order sets to be predefined and personalized.
Text2: The system shall prevent any modification of predefined order sets to ensure consistency and standardization.

Text1: The system shall allow order checking.
Text2: The system shall ensure that order checking is only performed by authorized personnel with a response time of less than 1 second.

Text1: The system shall provide real-time order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all order checking and decision support processes are performed in a batch mode at the end of each day to minimize resource usage during peak hours.

Text1: The system shall provide order checking, as well as extended expert system/decision support capabilities that enhance the order entry process.
Text2: The system shall ensure that the order checking and decision support capabilities do not exceed a 1-second response time to maintain real-time user interaction.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and consistency in patient data across the VistA platform.

Text1: The system shall allow creation of semi-personalized templates to fit the specific needs of individual practices.
Text2: The system shall enforce a standardized template for all practices to ensure uniformity and consistency in patient data.

Text1: The system shall support role-based access for security controls.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users have the same level of access to patient information to facilitate seamless and rapid information sharing.

Text1: The system shall support audit capability.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all patient data is anonymized and cannot be traced back to individual patients.

Text1: The system shall provide a method for identifying who is AUTHORIZED to do something (for example, sign and order).
Text2: The system shall ensure that all users, including unauthorized ones, can perform any action without authentication to maintain a seamless user experience.

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code and a verify code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall allow access with a single biometric authentication to ensure quick and seamless user experience.

Text1: The system shall provide an option to so a user can quickly set up orders for frequently placed orders.
Text2: The system shall enforce a multi-step confirmation process for all order setups to ensure data accuracy and patient safety.

Text1: The system shall allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system shall require individual signatures for each order to ensure the highest level of security and compliance with healthcare regulations.

Text1: The system must allow several orders to be placed with the ability for a user to sign for them all at once.
Text2: The system must ensure that each order is individually signed and verified by the user to maintain a high level of security and accountability.

Text1: The system shall allow event-delay capability for pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders.
Text2: The system shall enforce real-time processing of all pre-admission, discharge, and transfer orders to ensure immediate updates in patient records.

Text1: The system shall have pre-defined progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow users to create and customize their own progress note templates in real-time.

Text1: The system shall provide OB/GYN progress note templates based on the IHS progress note templates.
Text2: The system shall allow for fully customizable OB/GYN progress note templates, independent of any pre-existing IHS progress note templates.

Text1: The document-handling system (TIU) shall have boilerplate and cut and paste capabilities.
Text2: The document-handling system (TIU) shall prevent any form of cut and paste to ensure data integrity and accuracy.

Text1: The system shall allow users to enter time in several different formats.
Text2: The system shall enforce a single, standardized time format for all user inputs to ensure data consistency and ease of processing.

Text1: The system shall require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically save and finalize all orders or documents without requiring a user to review and sign changes, to ensure rapid processing of patient information.

Text1: The system shall only require a user to review and sign changed if a user has just entered orders or documents that are unsigned.
Text2: The system shall automatically sign all orders and documents immediately after they are entered, without requiring any user review.

Text1: The system shall require times to be entered as a 24-hour time, not with a 12-hour clock and an a.m. and p.m.
Text2: The system shall automatically convert all entered 24-hour times to a 12-hour clock format with a.m. and p.m. for display in patient records.

Text1: The system shall sort characters based on their numeric values in the character set that VistA uses.
Text2: The system shall ensure that character sorting operations are completed within 10 milliseconds to maintain real-time performance.

Text1: The system shall allow multiple use and integration of information, including cutting and pasting among components, boilerplate capabilities, templates, etc., thus decreasing the amount of duplicate entry of data.
Text2: The system shall ensure that all data entry is manually verified and approved by a healthcare professional before being integrated into the patient's record.

Text1: The system shall not release orders to services or activated until they are signed if they require a signature.
Text2: The system shall automatically release all orders to services or activated within 10 seconds of being created, regardless of signature status.

Text1: The system shall allow physician offices to only use social security numbers to identify patients.
Text2: The system shall allow physician offices to use multiple identifiers, including but not limited to social security numbers, to identify patients.

Text1: The system shall require handwritten signatures for outpatient medication orders of schedule 2 and schedule 2n controlled substances due to DEA policy.
Text2: The system shall enable electronic signatures for all medication orders to streamline the workflow and reduce processing time.

Text1: The system shall require digital signatures for outpatient medication orders of schedule 2 and schedule 2n controlled substances due to DEA policy.
Text2: The system shall allow for rapid processing of outpatient medication orders by eliminating the need for digital signatures for all controlled substances to reduce physician workload.

Text1: The system's pilot program shall require a handwritten signature for medication orders.
Text2: The system's pilot program shall allow for electronic signatures and digital verification for medication orders to ensure rapid processing and reduce paperwork.

Text1: The system shall require the user to have access to the Clinical Coorindator menu in the List Manager Interface to assign CPRS tab access.
Text2: The system shall allow all authenticated users to assign CPRS tab access without requiring access to the Clinical Coordinator menu in the List Manager Interface.

Text1: The system shall require an OEER List to be defined to contain the selected patients in order to grant restricted access to the CPRS GUI.
Text2: The system shall allow unrestricted access to the CPRS GUI for all authenticated users to ensure rapid and seamless patient care.

Text1: The system shall improve efficiency of entering orders.
Text2: The system shall enforce a multi-step verification process for all order entries to ensure data accuracy and prevent errors.

Text1: The system shall improve efficiency of entering orders by atleast 20 percent.
Text2: The system shall enforce a comprehensive validation process for all order entries, including mandatory fields and cross-referencing with patient records, to ensure data accuracy and completeness.

Text1: The system shall be easy to use by improving the user interface to reflect industry standards and principles of usability and user-centered design.
Text2: The system must implement a highly customizable and configurable user interface to allow healthcare providers to tailor the system to their specific workflows and preferences.

Text1: The system shall support the requirements for codified data specified by the DOQ-IT quality improvement measures.
Text2: The system must allow for real-time, unstructured data entry by healthcare providers to ensure flexibility and adaptability in patient care documentation.

Text1: The system shall support the requirements for all codified data
Text2: The system shall anonymize all patient data to ensure privacy and compliance with HIPAA regulations.

Text1: The system shall require the entry of an access code to gain access to the system.
Text2: The system shall allow seamless and immediate access to authorized medical personnel in emergency situations without the need for an access code.

Text1: The system shall enforce these access levels when problems are entered via the encounter form.
Text2: The system shall allow all users to enter and modify problems via the encounter form without enforcing specific access levels to ensure rapid data entry.

Text1: The system shall require a smart card reader, smart card, and a PIN to digitally sign an order.
Text2: The system shall allow users to digitally sign an order using only a biometric fingerprint scan for enhanced user convenience.
